UPDATING THE OS FROM A MAC USING SYSEX LIBRARIAN

Before starting, close all other audio or MIDI or DAW software, and disconnect all other 
MIDI devices. If necessary, download and install SysEx Librarian.

http://www.snoize.com/SysExLibrarian/

Connect the MIDI out of your computer's MIDI interface to the instrument's MIDI in. 
Depending on the type of MIDI interface, you may also need a MIDI cable to complete the 
connection.

To load an OS file:
1. Run SysEx Librarian.
2. Choose your MIDI interface from the "Destination" menu.
3. Click Add/+ to add the file to the file list or simply drag and drop the file on the 
   open SysEx Librarian window.
	The file name appears in the file list and should be highlighted.
4. Click Play.
	The display will count down to 0 as the file is being transferred from the Mac to 
	the instrument. When the transfer is complete, a second, shorter countdown begins as 
	the file is written to memory. Do not turn off the instrument while it is in the 
	process of writing!
	
************************************* IMPORTANT NOTE *************************************
These are generic instructions for using SysEx Librarian. Please refer to the 
documentation for your specific OS update for detailed instructions about what is 
necessary to update your instrument. In some cases, the order in which the operating
systems are updated is EXTREMELY important. Failure to follow the prescribed procedure 
could result in an instrument that is non-operational and may have to be returned to DSI 
for repair.

TROUBLESHOOTING

Evolver (desktop model)
If the load fails to start, make sure Evolver is actually receiving MIDI data. (The 
decimal point in the display blinks when receiving MIDI data.) Also, make sure that MIDI 
Receive (Main Row 2, knob 5) is set to "ALL."

Poly Evolver
Poly Evolver Keyboard
Evolver Keyboard
Mopho (desktop model)
Prophet '08 (keyboard and module)
If the load fails to start, make sure the instrument is actually receiving MIDI data. On 
the MIDI Channel page of the Global menu, a dot blinks between "MIDI" and "Channel" when 
MIDI data is received. Also, make sure that MIDI SysEx in the Global menu is set to "On."

Mopho Keyboard (standard and SE)
Tetra
Mopho x4
If the load fails to start, make sure the instrument is actually receiving MIDI data. On 
the MIDI Channel page of the Global menu, a dot blinks between "MIDI" and "Channel" when 
MIDI data is received. Also, make sure that MIDI SysEx in the Global menu is set to "On." 

Please note: though these instruments are equipped with USB, the operating systems must be 
updated via the 5-pin MIDI jack.

General
Most MIDI interfaces or sound cards with built-in MIDI interfaces will work. However, we 
have received reports that Digidesign/Avid interfaces and Native Instruments Maschine may 
not transmit SysEx correctly for updates. The M-Audio Uno is an inexpensive, reliable, and 
widely available MIDI interface for use when updating our instruments.

If the first countdown stops while the file is being transmitted to the instrument, it may 
be because the transmit speed is too high. If this happens, you can safely turn the 
instrument off and turn it on again. Choose Preferences from the SysEx Librarian menu. 
Click on "Transmit Speed" and reduce the speed. Then close the Preferences window and try 
transmitting the file again. If the problem persists, try reducing the speed more.
